heroHeadline: Trump Arrives Beijing for May 14-15 Xi Summit; PLA Drops to 2 Sorties on Summit Eve After 9 on May 12; HIMARS Deadline 18 Days Away — Taiwan Watches for Arms Sales Concessions
heroSubtitle: US President Trump arrived in Beijing on May 13, 2026, ahead of the May 14-15 Trump-Xi Jinping summit — the highest-stakes US-China bilateral meeting since Biden-era diplomacy, with Taiwan's security at the center of negotiations. PLA executed a summit-eve pullback to just 2 aircraft sorties on May 13 (down from 9 sorties on May 12, 5 of which crossed the median line into SW/Eastern ADIZ), while maintaining 7 PLAN vessels and 1 official ship — consistent with PLA's established pre-summit de-escalation choreography. The full May sortie sequence now reads: 4 (May 1) → 29 record (May 2) → 1 (May 3) → 2 (May 4) → 1 (May 5) → 0 (May 6) → 22 (May 7) → 12 (May 8) → 8 (May 9) → 12 (May 10) → 7 (May 11) → 9 (May 12) → 2 (May 13). Summit-eve analyses from CNBC, Foreign Policy, and Al Jazeera confirm Xi Jinping plans to press Trump on three Taiwan demands: (1) limiting future US arms sales to Taiwan, (2) opposing formal Taiwan independence, and (3) no senior US official visits to Taipei. The $14 billion PAC-3 MSE/NASAMS arms package remains on formal hold pending summit outcome, and Taiwan's HIMARS payment deadline is now 18 days away (May 31). Taiwan Deputy FM Francois Wu's defining warning — 'What we are most afraid of is to put Taiwan on the menu' — encapsulates Taipei's summit anxiety. Bipartisan US senators Shaheen/Tillis and Representatives Tiffany/Smith urged Trump (May 11) not to trade Taiwan's security for trade concessions, while Trump has publicly stated he will raise US arms sales to Taiwan and the Jimmy Lai imprisonment at the summit.
